papers.title: RaspAssistant as an Agentic Framework for Automating Adsorption Simulation Research in Porous Materials
papers.summary: Porous-material adsorption studies require coordinated structure preparation, force-field selection, simulation, validation, and interpretation, making end-to-end automation difficult. We test whether RaspAssistant, a hierarchical multi-agent framework, can carry an adsorption study from force-field preparation through validation and downstream separation analysis. Across twelve multi-agent workflow-reproduction runs spanning four adsorption and separation benchmarks, overall scores ranged from 8.50 to 10.00 on a rubric evaluating workflow correctness, simulation validity, and analysis consistency. In a separate eight-case force-field extraction benchmark, the mean weighted score was 0.967, combining parameter agreement and RASPA readiness. In open-ended studies, the system diagnosed and refined an acetylene force field and, after validating a CO$_2$ force field against MFI experiments, screened 197 pure-silica zeolites that passed automated input checks. These results demonstrate autonomous workflow execution after task specification and input provision: RaspAssistant coordinates, validates, adapts, and documents extended adsorption-simulation workflows while exposing model sensitivity and methodological limitations for expert review.

papers.title: Human–Agent Symbiotic Cognitive Architecture (HASCA): A Pair-Centric Framework for Longitudinal Human–Agent Co-Reasoning
papers.summary: Human–Agent Symbiotic Cognitive Architecture (HASCA) is a proposed pair-centric research framework originated by Goshtasb Gholami for investigating sustained collaboration between human decision-makers and AI agents while preserving distinct identities, human cognitive autonomy, and meaningful decision-making authority. The framework integrates several research components: Layered Reasoning Scaffold (LRS): Human-first reasoning, assumption testing, constructive disagreement, alternative-hypothesis exploration, and preservation of human decision ownership. Pair Reflection Audit (PRA): Longitudinal examination of human and agent contributions, inappropriate reliance, over-assistance, and cognitive autonomy. Governed Pair Memory: A proposed framework for provenance-aware, permission-sensitive, temporally revisable interaction memory. Reciprocal Revision: Ongoing correction of human and agent working models, with attention to epistemic benefits and the costs of disagreement. The planned research program includes a controlled feasibility study comparing unaided human reasoning, conventional AI assistance, and LRS-assisted reasoning, with independent no-AI transfer assessment. Subsequent studies would investigate persistent memory, reflective feedback, and longitudinal collaboration. HASCA is currently a conceptual and technical research program. papers.title: PIU Smart Intelligence Agents: Design and Implementation of a Security-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture for Enterprise Intelligence
papers.summary: Enterprises increasingly rely on heterogeneous documents, relational databases, and analytical systems to support information retrieval and business decision-making. Integrating large language models (LLMs) with these sources introduces challenges in evidence reliability, analytical correctness, access control, and operational resilience. This paper presents PIU Smart Intelligence Agents, a security-aware multi-agent architecture designed to integrate enterprise document intelligence, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, document summarization, naturallanguage-to-SQL analytics, key performance indicator (KPI) generation, and conversational AI within a common application and governance framework. The proposed architecture organizes specialized AI capabilities around shared services for authentication, authorization, request validation, provider integration, observability, and controlled data access. Its document-processing workflow encompasses file validation, text extraction, optical character recognition for scanned documents, normalization, chunking, embedding generation, and vector-based indexing. The structured-analytics workflow separates schema-aware query generation from SQL validation, restricted database execution, and result interpretation. The architecture also addresses provider compatibility, timeout handling, failure recovery, document lifecycle

papers.title: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning
papers.summary: Agentic system design is increasingly shifting from hand-crafted prompts and workflows toward automated search over agentic programs and interaction structures, with multi-agent systems receiving growing attention. Yet a central question remains unresolved: when does an automatically generated multi-agent structure exhibit a functionally meaningful division of responsibility? We argue that automated multi-agent design should move beyond searching for effective architectures toward identifying which responsibilities are functionally necessary, how they should be allocated, and when they should change. To explore this, we propose Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD), which treats organization itself as a first-class design object, explicitly modeling how agent teams are composed, what functional responsibilities the agents assume, how they coordinate, and how collective decisions are made. We formulate AMOD as an execution-driven design loop. For each task, an automated designer instantiates an organization by assigning functional responsibilities and coordination rules to a set of agents. After execution, task outcomes, intermediate artifacts, and interaction traces are examined to identify which responsibilities may be missing, duplicated, or ineffective, and the organization is revised accordingly. papers.title: A PRIVACY PRESERVING PERSONAL AI ASSISTANT AND THE COST OF CLOUD MODEL INFERENCE: ARCHITECTURE, CAPABILITY TRADEOFFS, AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
papers.summary: Personal AI assistants need reliable research and controlled access to private data. This report specifies a local-first Windows architecture and examines the capability, privacy, and operating-cost tradeoff between local Llama 3.2 3B through Ollama and self-hosted Kimi K2.5 on rented NVIDIA GPUs. We analyzed a supplied project design summary, mapped trust boundaries and failure modes, and calculated illustrative costs from a documented eight-H200 deployment and published rental rates. The design separates public research from authenticated browser sessions, enforces permissions outside the model, and requires evidence-supported answers. At an illustrative $4.59 per GPU-hour, eight H200s cost $36.72 per running hour, $4,406.40 for four hours daily over 30 days, or $26,438.40 for continuous 30-day operation, before storage and operations. An assumed 100 W incremental local draw for four hours daily at $0.15/kWh costs $1.80 monthly on an existing PC. These are scenarios, not measured deployments. Kimi K2.5 offers multimodal and agentic capabilities that a text-only 3B baseline should not be assumed to match; no matched end-to-end test was performed. Stronger cloud inference can impose substantial dedicated GPU rental cost and transfers prompts to a cloud operator. Local inference preserves a narrower data boundary at far lower incremental cash cost but requires direct task-qualit

papers.title: Review of System Design Approaches in Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Security Operations Centers
papers.summary: Security operations centers increasingly rely on agentic artificial intelligence systems, which combine large language model reasoning with tool invocation and multi-step planning, to automate alert triage, investigation, and response. Independent research groups have proposed structurally distinct architectures for this purpose, ranging from single-agent reasoning loops to multi-agent systems with shared context or deterministic safety constraints, but no publication has systematically compared these designs against a common set of criteria. This review addresses that gap by constructing a five-dimension classification framework covering agent cardinality, coordination mechanism, autonomy boundary, safety enforcement layer, and validation maturity. A corpus of published systems relevant to security operations was retrieved from academic preprint archives and conference proceedings and coded against this framework. Five recurring design patterns were identified, together with the available quantitative evidence comparing them, including a controlled trial showing that multi-agent orchestration produced consistently reliable recommendations while single-agent approaches did not. The analysis found that claimed autonomy consistently outpaced empirical validation across the reviewed designs, with most systems evaluated no further than a single organizational deployment despite per

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
papers.summary: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. papers.title: Performance Evaluation and Late Blight Reaction of Advanced Potato Genotypes for Yield and Quality Traits in Bekoji, Southeastern Ethiopia
papers.summary: The research aimed to assess potato genotypes that possess high yield and tuber quality characteristics and yield traits. The study was arranged by randomized complete block design with three replications and was executed at the Bekoji substation during the main cropping seasons of 2022 and 2023. The results revealed that all the traits except days emergence showed significant differences among the genotypes. The genotypes varied for dry matter content, specific gravity, and total starch content, which ranged from 18.32% to 23.66%, 1.07 to 1.097 g/cm^3^, and 12.03% to 17.08%, respectively. The genotype CIP315009. 71 had the highest specific gravity, dry matter content, and total starch content. The four advanced clones CIP315003.132, CIP315008.30, CIP315009.71, and CIP315004.61 produced a total tuber yield that exceeded the released variety, Burka. The identified genotypes may provide useful breeding material for improving yield and processing-related tuber quality.

papers.title: The Show-Up Attack: When Subagents Win Over Their Supervisor
papers.summary: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed to coordinate multiple large language model (LLM) agents. However, this also creates new attack surfaces: malicious agents may have chances to exploit the coordination. In this paper, we propose and study the \textit{show-up attack}, in which a malicious subagent manipulates the supervisor into involving it in tasks beyond its assigned scope. To evaluate this risk, we propose SUA-Arena, which implements 6 attack strategies and contains 188 test cases. Then, we evaluate 6 frontier LLMs and find that all of them are vulnerable to show-up attacks. For example, GPT-5.6-Sol as a supervisor suffers an ASR of up to 0.93. Mitigation strategies such as prompting and restricted communication fail to reduce the risk consistently. These results show that multi-agent systems need explicit mechanisms for enforcing authority boundaries.

papers.title: Authoring and Management of Transparent Research Integrity Assessments of Randomised Clinical Trial Publications Using LLM-Assisted Tools and Provenance Knowledge Graphs
Energy-aware and AI-enabled offloading framework in edge-to-cloud continuum
papers.summary: The rapid expansion of the Edge-to-Cloud (EOC) computing continuum has enabled a new generation of distributed, low-latency applications by pushing computation closer to data sources through edge and fog nodes. However, the heterogeneity of these environments, device-level energy constraints, and the absence of sustainability-aware optimisation models make accurate device-health and performance prediction, task scheduling, and computation offloading extremely challenging. Existing offloading approaches are typically designed around single-objective optimisation and only limited work considers device degradation or sustainability factors. This thesis addresses these limitations through three integrated contributions. Firstly, it introduces LiRUL, a lightweight edge-deployable model for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of Lithium-ion batteries. Battery degradation directly affects device reliability, energy availability, and offloading feasibility; therefore, accurate RUL estimation is essential for sustainable and health-aware decision-making. By combining degradation-sensitive features with efficient temporal learning, LiRUL provides accurate health estimation with minimal overhead. Although LiRUL is developed as an independent contribution, its predictions provide the foundational device-health information that future offloading frameworks can exploit to avoid unreliable

papers.title: TME LLM OS: A Closed-Loop Systems Engineering Architecture for Epistemic Correction in AI Agent Systems Systems Engineering Proposal
From Artificial Intelligence to Institutional Intelligence
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence and agentic systems can redistribute reading, research, synthesis, criticism, drafting, and coordination within courts. This article asks how that redistribution changes judicial cognition and which institutional safeguards are needed to preserve legitimate adjudication. Through an interdisciplinary narrative review and doctrinal analysis, it develops a framework of institutional intelligence anchored in Brazilian National Council of Justice Resolution No. 615/2025, as amended by Resolution No. 674/2026. Five categories organize the argument: institutional cognitive space describes the allocation of cognitive work; artificial adversariality identifies structured internal challenge among agents; the institutional rein integrates controls over delegated autonomy; meaningful human initiative emphasizes the continuing human authority to frame problems and determine purposes; and institutional AI curation describes the competence required to select, validate, contextualize, and reject artificial contributions. Recent research on human–AI collaboration and multi-agent failure qualifies the framework: neither human review nor artificial disagreement guarantees reliability, and short-term performance gains do not establish long-term professional competence. The article distinguishes technical auditability from legal reason-giving and internal agent de

papers.title: AI-supported virtual laboratory for flipped physics learning: effects on middle school students’ achievement, motivation, and cognitive load
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of an AI-supported virtual laboratory (AI-VL) on middle school students’ flipped physics learning. A pretest–posttest control-group quasi-experimental design was adopted with 90 Grade 9 students from a middle school in central China. Three intact classes were assigned to the AI-VL, virtual laboratory (VL), and physical laboratory (PL) groups, with 30 students in each group. ANCOVA revealed large group effects on physics learning achievement, F (2, 86) = 113.38, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.73, and overall learning motivation, F (2, 86) = 113.37, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.73. The AI-VL group outperformed the VL and PL groups, while the VL group also outperformed the PL group. The AI-VL group reported higher intrinsic motivation, whereas the group difference in extrinsic motivation was not statistically significant ( p = 0.054). Significant group differences were also found across the three cognitive load dimensions, with F (2, 87) values ranging from 9.07 to 72.94 and partial η 2 values ranging from 0.17 to 0.63. The AI-VL group reported the lowest perceived intrinsic cognitive load and the highest germane cognitive load, while both AI-VL and VL resulted in lower extraneous cognitive load than PL. papers.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
papers.summary: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models. We argue that interface design should itself be an agent capability. We introduce Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that builds Evolving Agent Interfaces from task experience. A meta-agent examines task agents' trajectories on synthetic training tasks, without success labels, and constructs and revises interfaces and usage knowledge in a repository. Population-based evolution then selects which repositories to develop further by their performance on validation tasks the meta-agent never sees, favoring changes that generalize beyond the seen tasks. On OSWorld V2, Agent S4, with Qwen3.8-27B and the evolved repository of interfaces, sets a new state of the art in open-source computer-use agents, reaching 21.3% binary score, 3.8 times the same model with fixed interfaces. This is above both GPT-5.5 (13.0%) and Claude Opus 4.8 (20.6%), at about 4.3% and 1.5% of their respective costs. On ScienceBoard, the evolved interfaces improve the success rate from 41.4% to 58.6% with the same model. These result

papers.title: InterWebCoder: Learning Interactive Webpage Generation from Executable Tests via Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Interactive webpages underpin modern applications, but reproducing both their visual appearance and multi-step behavior remains challenging for multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Scalable training data must capture user actions, state transitions, and expected outcomes, while real-world webpage code is often entangled with irrelevant scripts and external dependencies. Moreover, existing GUI-agent-based verification provides slow and potentially unstable functional feedback. To address these challenges, we propose InterWebCoder, an efficient framework for interactive webpage code generation. InterWebCoder introduces a Test-Specification-Guided and Execution-Verified Data Synthesis pipeline that records real-world interaction trajectories and synthesizes self-contained webpage code with executable test scripts. A failureattributed repair mechanism uses runtime evidence to locate and iteratively fix errors in either the webpage code or test script. We then combine test-ID-weighted supervised fine-tuning with group-relative policy optimization, directly optimizing functional correctness and visual fidelity using test pass rates and state-level visual similarity. This replaces costly GUI-agent verification with fast, reproducible executable feedback. Our pipeline produces 1,736 verified samples from 2,058 tasks, achieving an 84.35% synthesis success rate. papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Variational Optimization of neuromorphic self-supervised heterogeneous graph transformers for multimodal Parkinson’s disease representation learning
papers.summary: Early diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease (PD) remains challenging due to the heterogeneous nature of multimodal clinical data, limited annotated datasets, suboptimal multimodal fusion strategies, and the absence of uncertainty-aware decision-making in existing deep learning models. This paper proposes NeuroQ-MGST, a Neuromorphic Self-Supervised Multimodal Graph Transformer with Quantum-Inspired Variational Optimization, for robust and interpretable PD diagnosis. The proposed framework integrates a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) encoder to capture temporally sparse modality-specific representations, a self-supervised contrastive and masked reconstruction objective to exploit unlabeled data, and a Dynamic Heterogeneous Graph Construction (DHGC) with a Hierarchical Multimodal Graph Transformer (HMGT) to model complex cross-modal interactions among speech, gait, neuroimaging, and clinical biomarkers. To improve optimization in highly non-convex multimodal learning spaces, a Quantum-Inspired Variational Optimization (QIVO) module performs structured global representation refinement, while a Bayesian Monte Carlo Dropout layer provides calibrated predictive uncertainty for confidence-aware clinical decision support. Experimental evaluation on the PMMD 2.0 and UCI Parkinson’s Disease datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework, achieving 98.7% accuracy and 98.9% AUC-R

papers.title: Pixels to precision: Deep learning in dental imaging
papers.summary: Dental imaging is fundamental to diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up in Oral Medicine and Maxillofacial Radiology. Although conventional radiographic interpretation remains dependent on professional expertise, diagnostic performance may be influenced by observer variability, image quality, workload, and the subtle nature of early pathological changes. The development of Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has introduced new approaches for automated analysis of dental and maxillofacial images. This narrative review discusses the evolution, principles, applications, clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions of deep learning in dental imaging, with emphasis on intraoral radiography, panoramic radiography, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), and related imaging modalities. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated applications in dental caries detection, periodontal bone assessment, periapical lesion detection, tooth identification and numbering, jaw lesion analysis, anatomical segmentation, and treatment planning. More advanced architectures, including U-Net, residual networks, object-detection models, three-dimensional CNNs, and emerging transformer-based systems, have expanded the scope of automated image interpretation. papers.title: The new constructionism. Papert after Peirce: indexicality, navigational thinking, and learning in the age of generative AI
papers.summary: The arrival of generative AI in every classroom has produced a crisis that is at once technological, epistemological, and pedagogical. We argue that the appropriate response is neither prohibition nor naive adoption, but a principled reconstruction of constructionism for a computational environment that is generative, context-sensitive, and dialogically accessible. Drawing on Peircean semiotics, Papertian constructionism, Polanyi's epistemology, and contemporary neural-network research, we develop a programmatic framework we call the New Constructionism. We make four connected contributions. First, we argue that generative AI introduces an indexical mode of computation: its relation to the empirical world may be direct, mediated, or incomplete, but in a situated human–AI configuration meaning is operationally conditioned by conversational history, artifacts, tools, observations, and action. Second, we introduce a three-dimensional analytical space — semiotic, psycho-epistemological, and pedagogical — in which learning paradigms can be located and compared. Third, we reinterpret the history of programming education as a movement from a predominantly symbolic environment toward a hybrid ecology in which symbolic execution, distributional generation, and situated reference coexist. This hybridity qualifies but does not cancel the indexical turn at the level of interaction and educ

papers.title: Common-sense thinking and decision making
papers.summary: Common-sense thinking (CST) is proposed as the dynamic, situation-responsive application of commonsense knowledge rather than the mere possession of static facts. This conceptual article distinguishes two modes of CST. System A applies an already adequate representation of a familiar situation, whereas System B becomes important when that representation must be constructed, adapted, or reconsidered. The distinction concerns the amount of situation-specific construction required rather than simply the speed or effort of reasoning. CST is related to, but distinguished from, neighbouring constructs and research traditions, including practical intelligence, executive functions, rational thinking, metacognition, wisdom, adaptive expertise, and Naturalistic Decision Making. Its central decision-theoretic contribution is the proposal that CST also functions at a meta-decision level: recognising when unaided judgement is adequate and when a problem requires more explicit structuring and decision analysis. Examples from scientific reasoning and professional practice illustrate how context-sensitive practical judgement may operate, while structured decision methods are viewed as complements to rather than replacements for such judgement. The framework is explicitly conceptual and remains to be empirically validated. Testable propositions are proposed concerning System B reasoning, indivi

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: A meaningful framework for change for the Police
papers.summary: Background This PhD project evolved from MSc research by the author into stressors in a UK police force. The findings from both the MSc study and existing literature suggested that the UK police need a new way to support their officers and staff in reducing psychological distress. This led the author to want to create a Meaningful Framework for Change, moving the police from being reactive to psychological distress to being proactive and preventative. Aim and Research Question This PhD project aimed to develop a Framework for Change within a specific UK police force to determine its feasibility and identify what might be required to achieve this goal. In this sense, the PhD project is somewhat untraditional, as the author is an applied psychologist and the work is hands-on and practical, involving support methods that are to be tried and tested within the pilot force. Methods Due to its applied and practical nature, the author was embedded with the pilot police force, and the most logical method for this project was to be autoethnographical in its approach. The thesis is subsequently written in the first person and is less traditional than the reader may be used to seeing. Results/Findings The findings showed that it is possible to design a Meaningful Framework for Change for a police force, introducing new methods of supporting officers and staff. papers.title: Developing a multisensory smell retraining programme
papers.summary: Olfactory training (OT) is a well-established intervention for enhancing smell function, but questions remain about the mechanisms underpinning its effectiveness and the features that optimise outcomes. This thesis investigates how factors such as odour pleasantness, training duration, subjective experiences, and multisensory integration contribute to OT efficacy, drawing on both quantitative and qualitative approaches. A systematic review of the OT literature revealed that improvements in olfactory function are influenced by elements such as training duration, odour selection, and adherence. However, the review also highlighted substantial methodological variation across studies, underscoring the need for more standardised and theory-driven approaches. To facilitate experimental control over odour valence in subsequent work, a stimulus set of pleasant and unpleasant odours was developed and validated through hedonic ratings, enabling precise manipulation of this dimension. Building on these foundations, a 16-week longitudinal OT study was conducted with participants with and without olfactory dysfunction who trained using a set of pleasant, unpleasant, or mixed odours. Results indicated that olfactory function improved over time regardless of odour valence, suggesting that a longer training duration may be more influential than odour pleasantness in driving improvement. papers.title: Intercultural competence under managed proximity: A relational account of student practices in a Sino-French partnership university
papers.summary: This study examines intercultural competence (ICC) as a situated practice emerging under conditions of what I term ‘managed proximity’ in a Sino–French partnership university during the COVID-19 campus lockdown. Managed proximity refers to the structural coordination of encounter through rules, routines, and infrastructures that brought students together while differentiating access and visibility. ICC is conceptualised as a context-sensitive practice which sustains communication and interaction among participants operating in their shared space of managed proximity. Empirically, the study draws on narrative interviews and reflective journals with eleven Chinese undergraduate students. Theoretically, it adopts a non-essentialist perspective on culture and brings Holliday’s Grammar of Culture into dialogue with Bourdieu’s theory of capital to examine how interaction across difference was organised through intersecting structural conditions, agentic responses, and contextually available resources. The examination explores how students interpreted rules, mediated access, absorbed procedural pressures, and coordinated with others across settings such as pandemic routines, classroom practices, digital access, and internship policy. papers.title: Islet extracellular matrix remodelling in type 2 diabetes: implications for β-cell failure and therapeutic opportunities
papers.summary: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterised by progressive insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, ultimately resulting in impaired glucose homeostasis. While metabolic and genetic factors are central to disease development, increasing evidence indicates that disruption of the pancreatic islet extracellular matrix (ECM) may be an important contributor to β-cell failure. The islet ECM is not merely a structural scaffold but a dynamic signalling network that regulates β-cell adhesion, survival, proliferation and insulin secretion through integrin-mediated signalling and mechanotransduction pathways. In healthy islets, a tightly organised ECM composed of collagens, laminins, fibronectin and glycosaminoglycans maintains basement membrane integrity, vascular support and coordinated cell-matrix communication. In T2DM, chronic hyperglycaemia, inflammation and oxidative stress are associated with pathological ECM remodelling and are thought to contribute to alterations in islet ECM composition characterised by fibrosis, altered matrix composition, dysregulated proteolysis and excessive ECM protein deposition. These changes are potentially associated with impaired integrin signalling, altered mechanotransduction and compromised β-cell function and viability in experimental models. papers.title: A lactate–mitochondrial axis framework for mild hyperthermia and checkpoint blockade in driver-negative NSCLC: testing temporal coupling
papers.summary: Metabolic constraints, including hypoxia, lactate, and adenosine that impair CD8 + T-cell function and mitochondrial fitness, are increasingly recognized as contributors to resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in driver-negative (lacking an established first-line actionable driver alteration) advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We propose a hypothesis-driven framework asking whether transient tissue-level metabolic relief can be temporally aligned with the slower process of T-cell reinvigoration driven by immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Its mechanistic basis is a lactate–mitochondrial axis linking extracellular metabolic suppression to mitochondrial states in tumor-infiltrating T cells, with T-cell-intrinsic mitochondrial adaptation treated as a testable extension. Locoregional mild hyperthermia (39–42 °C) is conceptualized as a transient modulator of tissue-level metabolic gradients rather than a direct immune activator. Because oxygenation, metabolite distribution, and acid–base status may change independently or in opposing directions, oxygenation is treated as a physiological readout rather than a surrogate for metabolic relief. We define a relief window as transient attenuation of hypoxic constraint accompanied by redistribution of lactate and adenosine away from T-cell-containing regions. papers.title: Argument-First Versus Language-First Generative AI Feedback in Chinese EFL Argumentative Writing: A Randomized Study
papers.summary: This eight-week randomized study examined how the order of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) feedback shaped revision and near-term independent writing among 132 Chinese English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) undergraduates. Students received argument-first (AF; n = 67) or language-first (LF; n = 65) feedback; 64 pairs underwent within-class, within-pair randomization, and four unmatched students were randomized within class. Both modules were independently generated from each initial draft (D0) and locked before release. Students completed two revisions (D1 and D2) across three tasks and a new-topic, AI-free transfer task. Adjusted AF–LF differences in D0–D2 change favored AF for overall quality (0.811 points, 95% CI [0.424, 1.198]) and argumentation (1.102 points, 95% CI [0.668, 1.536]), but not language quality (0.020 points, 95% CI [−0.381, 0.420]). Revision depth and implementation showed stage-specific crossovers. Language contrasts did not survive primary Holm adjustment, although complete-pair sensitivity analysis detected a crossover. Argumentation transfer favored AF (1.057 points, 95% CI [0.508, 1.606]); overall transfer was less consistent, with the complete-pair interval including zero (0.685 points, 95% CI [−0.111, 1.481]). papers.title: Open Educational Resources as Enabling Conditions for Student Resilience to Failure and Uncertainty
papers.summary: As today's scientific challenges become increasingly complex and interdisciplinary, future researchers in the fields of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) need both disciplinary skills and adaptive resilience to persevere and cope productively with failure. We argue that Open Educational Resources (OER) provide the enabling conditions for this resilience. OER are freely accessible and openly licensed materials that can be reused, adapted, and redistributed without cost barriers. In comparison to closed educational resources, OER provide greater flexibility in learning by enabling students to access a broader range of materials beyond a single prescribed textbook, work at their own pace, and revisit or compare content as needed. Such flexibility may reduce learning-related anxiety and foster persistence when facing academic difficulty. Drawing on resilience theory (e.g., Dweck's growth mindset, Henry et al.'s FAIL framework) and experiences from the Community of Practice “Innovation in STEM Education” (University of Groningen, Netherlands), this paper explores how OER's unique characteristics such as their adaptability, accessibility, and diversity of materials serve as enabling conditions that foster students' tolerance of failure and uncertainty.
